title: Review WHO DEP1 as an antidepressant baseline
proposedRouting: Compare WHO DEP1 with the existing CANMAT antidepressant ticket, the starter formulary, and medication-specific safety or fit files before changing the MDD family or patient rubric.
guidance: WHO DEP1 conditionally considers a defined group of SSRIs or amitriptyline for moderate-to-severe depression, with very low certainty. Its implementation notes make selection context-sensitive and emphasize adverse effects, availability, psychosocial care, and patient preferences. Decide what this contributes as a broad non-specialist baseline; do not infer that unlisted agents are ineffective or that one listed SSRI is uniquely optimal.
resurfacingTrigger: When the MDD diagnostic/severity standard, starter formulary, antidepressant catalog, or a more specific initial-treatment guideline changes.

title: Design a later antidepressant-continuation patient from WHO DEP2
proposedRouting: Use DEP2 as a candidate source for a distinct best-next-step template involving benefit, remission, adherence, adverse effects, continuation, and safe discontinuation; do not inject duration logic into the initial-treatment patient.
guidance: WHO DEP2 conditionally supports continuing a beneficial antidepressant for at least six months after remission with regular monitoring, but the certainty is very low and the section identifies unanswered duration and withdrawal questions. Decide which patient states and decisions belong in a future continuation encounter and which require more specific guidance before scoring.
resurfacingTrigger: When continuation, relapse prevention, tapering, withdrawal, or recurrence-count guidance is added.

title: Map WHO DEP3 to discrete psychotherapy entries
proposedRouting: Compare DEP3 with the current therapy catalog and the CANMAT psychotherapy ticket. Add missing therapy definitions separately and audit whether the current broad psychotherapy and behavioral-activation rows double count one modality.
guidance: WHO DEP3 strongly supports a set of structured psychological interventions for moderate-to-severe depression with moderate certainty and does not include nondirective supportive counseling in that recommendation. Decide which therapy IDs satisfy a broad pathway, which need new catalog files, and whether availability or patient fit belongs in separate modifiers.
resurfacingTrigger: When therapy catalog entries, therapy availability, or structured-psychotherapy guidance changes.

title: Resolve WHO DEP4 treatment-modality implications
proposedRouting: Compare the structured patient severity, treatment availability, and preferences with WHO DEP4 and the existing CANMAT modality ticket before defining database-plan and engine-inferred routes.
guidance: WHO DEP4 conditionally describes psychological intervention or combined treatment for moderate-to-severe depression as preference- and benefit/harm-sensitive, with antidepressant monotherapy considered when psychological intervention is unavailable. Decide whether the current patient supports psychotherapy alone, combined care, medication alone, or multiple routes; preserve availability as a structured fact rather than assuming it.
resurfacingTrigger: When severity facts, treatment availability, preferences, or initial-modality guidance changes.
